solution:
Correct option: (c) Political parties.

The chapter says that when people form organisations aiming at achieving political power and participating in the electoral process, such organisations are called political parties. It adds that political parties can be described as a group of people who aim to contest elections, win them, get power and establish the government of their party.

solution:
Correct option: (c) Dravid Munnetra Kazhagam.

The chapter’s information box opens: ‘Justice Party - a non Brahmin movement in 1920 was transformed into Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam - a political party.’

Note that the same box then says the Justice Party came to be known as Dravida Kazhagam in 1944 and that a group separated from it in 1949 to establish the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, so the box is not internally consistent. Only one Dravidian party is offered among the options, so the answer itself is not in doubt.
